audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart directly contradicted the already-audited mirror. Our page read Skill / Swain / Swain / Skill / Skill / Swain / Swain; the mirror (aurora__swain) was set as one atomic group to Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Skill, and the packet chart agrees with the mirror.
audit.why: Mirrors must be inverse-consistent, and our own whys[1] through whys[5] already describe Aurora as the favourite at every one of those stages — the side tokens were the only thing disagreeing with the page's own prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped to Aurora and row 6 to Skill in both layers as matched pairs, with ratings dropped from 5/6 to 4 across the Aurora rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'mid' told the reader that spending her hop gives 'that is your 10-second window'. The Weirding is 15/14/13/12/11s, and Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s. No real cooldown appeared anywhere else on the page.
audit.why: A five-second error on the one cooldown the advice is keyed to gets the reader killed stepping up too late.
audit.corrected: 15s and 22s written into mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, whys[1] and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanical errors. (a) Across the Veil was described as a 'spirit exile' that 'removes her from the fight for a full second' and dodges Demonflare — it grants invisibility and move speed, not untargetability, and Swain's Vision of Empire carries revealsStealth, which strips it. The page never mentioned the reveal once. (b) Her escape was repeatedly called an 'E blink'; The Weirding is a slow-blast with a backward hop, and the actual leap is Across the Veil (W).
audit.why: Riot's text: W 'entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible'; Swain W 'Champions hit are revealed'. Invisibility does not prevent AoE damage from a Demonflare nova.
audit.corrected: The reveal stated in spikes[1].text, mid, report[5].t and dosFull[2].d; wants.foe[2] no longer claims the leap dodges the nova.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell she lands and anti-heal was never mentioned in the trading text.
audit.why: Her passive sustain is what wins the poke war the page tells you to contest.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now names Spirit Abjuration and Grievous Wounds timing.

edits.before: Aurora's W spirit exile removes her from the fight for a full second, meaning she can dodge your R Demonflare nova and exit your drain range the moment you pop Ascension.
edits.after: Across the Veil (22s) leaps her away invisible, not untargetable — Vision of Empire reveals her through it, so W the landing spot and she cannot break your drain.

edits.before: Use W spirit exile to exit Demonic Ascension drain range and dodge Demonflare's nova on recast
edits.after: Leap out with Across the Veil to break your drain range before Demonflare's nova lands

edits.before: Aurora hits level 2 and gains her E blink, which cleanly dodges your E root on reaction — she can now nullify your entire engage pattern and is safer than you.
edits.after: Aurora hits level 2 and The Weirding (15s) slows you and hops her back out of the return pass — she blunts your whole engage pattern and is simply safer than you.

edits.before: From levels 4 through 6 Aurora owns this lane because she has more consistent poke tools and her blink keeps her safe from every all-in you have. Play around her E cooldown: if you see her use the blink to dodge a minion wave or reposition, that is your 10-second window to step forward and throw W-E. At level 6 your R gives you sustain in extended fights, but her W spirit exile lets her literally leave the fight for a second and re-enter when Demonflare is already cast — she does not have to eat the nova. Use R to sustain through her Q poke and deny her the attrition win, not to force an all-in she can blink and exile out of.
edits.after: From levels 4 through 6 Aurora owns this lane because she has more consistent poke tools and her hop keeps her safe from every all-in you have. Play around The Weirding: it is 15s at rank 1, so the moment you see her spend it to reposition, that is your window to step forward and throw W-E. At level 6 your R gives you sustain in extended fights, and Across the Veil (22s) only makes her invisible — Vision of Empire reveals her, so drop W on her landing spot and the escape buys her nothing. Use R to sustain through her Q poke and deny her the attrition win, not to force an all-in she can hop out of.

edits.before: - Aurora Twofold Hex: matchup-defining — Her escape. E-root when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Aurora The Weirding: matchup-defining — a 15s slow-and-hop escape, and Across the Veil hides her for 22s. Track both before every engage. - Your E: 12s, never on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Aurora's Twofold Hex (Blink): Her escape. E-root when it’s down. When it is down — E-root + R her.
edits.after: Across the Veil hides her, it does not untarget her — your W reveals it. The Weirding is 15s at rank 1.

edits.before: Aurora wastes Twofold Hex (Blink) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Your W reveals her out of Across the Veil — poke it, then commit.

edits.before: That is Aurora's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell she lands — get Grievous Wounds early.

notes: 'Twofold Hex (Blink)' appears throughout both layers as her escape. Twofold Hex is her Q, a curse missile with a recast — it is not a blink. I corrected it where the string was matchup-specific; it survives in ahead, loading, focus.text, breakdown.early/mid/trading/spikes/feeding/difficulty, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[9].t, report[10].t, report[12].t, report[13].t and dosFull[0], which are shared boilerplate. focus.text ('Aurora Twofold Hex', 18 chars) is under the applier's 25-character skip threshold and cannot be fixed by an edit at all.
